title: Hormuz, Liquidity, and Upcoming Investments
summary: Selective deployment amid an energy shock.
assessment: Micron’s directional breakout and Visa’s business resilience receive support. HDFC’s operating recovery is weaker and its ADR underperforms over the audit window. A sentiment observation is misdated, and attribution of weak hiring to AI remains unproven. The report appropriately qualifies possible price bottoms, which should not be scored as guaranteed floors.

claims.claim: Poorer importers face greater energy shortages.
claims.reason: The affordability mechanism is plausible and the extended shock is confirmed, but relative physical rationing depends on subsidies, currency reserves, contracts and domestic production. Income alone does not rank realized damage.

evidence.title: September oil market report
evidence.finding: Severe disruption persisted into August; cumulative observed oil inventory draws since February reached 507 million barrels.

claims.next_check: Compare import-dependent countries by inventories, fuel availability and real-income losses.

coverage_note: Full numbered text and image inventory read. All material theses across macro, digital assets, investment analysis and concluding sections considered. Position listings and incidental descriptive statistics are excluded unless they support a thesis.
framework_lessons: Distinguish option income from stock upside.
verification_limitations: Current page snapshot is not an authenticated publication-date version.
A missing horizon is not replaced with an invented author deadline.
Market sensitivities use vendor adjusted closes and do not reconstruct portfolio execution.
